content.text: This is how 7'9 (2.36m) Olivier Rioux does his basketball pregame workout training, by touching the backboard without even jumping. At 7'9 (2.36m), Olivier Rioux is the world’s tallest basketball player, and this video shows how he prepares with an intense pregame workout routine. From strength training, conditioning drills, mobility exercises, and basketball skills development, Olivier’s pregame workout highlights the importance of athletic performance, professional fitness training, and mental preparation at the highest level of competition. This video is perfect for anyone interested in basketball training, sports performance, athlete conditioning, health & wellness, and professional fitness routines. Learn how discipline, recovery, nutrition, and workout consistency help athletes like Rioux succeed on the court. ▶️ Olivier Rioux is a Canadian college basketball player for the Florida Gators of the Southeastern Conference (SEC). Guinness World Records declared him the tallest teenager in the world in 2021, he measured 7 ft 5 in (2.26 m) at age 15. He now stands 7 ft 9 in (2.36 m) tall. Olivier Rioux was born in Terrebonne on February 2, 2006, to Jean-François, a 6 ft 8 in (2.03 m) photographer and former volleyball player, and Anne Gariépy, who is 6 ft 1 in (1.85 m), and works at the Royal Bank of Canada (RBC). His 6 ft 9 in (2.06 m) older brother, Émile, has also played basketball. The family has resided in the Anjou borough of Montreal and the suburb of Beloeil. Both Olivier and Émile played for multiple Canadian AAU teams. Olivier Rioux first gained attention while playing internationally for the French Phenoms at age 12 when he was 6 ft 10 in (2.08 m). He played for Real Madrid and Brookwood Elite prior to attending IMG Academy. Olivier Rioux committed to play college basketball at the University of Florida. He did not appear in any of the Gators' first four games of the 2024–25 season. After the fourth game, head coach Todd Golden told the Associated Press that Olivier Rioux was being redshirted, and that he had previously discussed the matter with Olivier Rioux, his family, and his AAU coach. Olivier Rioux is one of the fan favorites as he will be the tallest player in college basketball history once he makes his debut. Olivier Rioux first represented Canada at youth level during the 2021 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship in Mexico. He helped Canada win bronze at the tournament, finishing with averages of 8.3 points and 10.3 rebounds per game. A year later, he played for Canada at the 2022 FIBA U17 World Cup in Spain. He finished the competition with averages of 2.7 points and 4.7 rebounds per game. In June 2023, Olivier Rioux was selected to play for Canada at the 2023 FIBA U19 World Cup in Hungary. He averaged 3.2 points and 3.4 rebounds per game over the course of the tournament. The following year, at the 2024 FIBA Under-18 AmeriCup in Argentina, Olivier Rioux won his second bronze medal at youth level. He finished the event averaging 4.5 points and 4.5 rebounds per game. #nba #basketball #olivier
